ops.title: spawnllm SIGTERMs only the direct child on timeout, leaking grandchildren
ops.description:
Found 2026-09-03 while bounding slop-cop's LLM retry loop. NOT fixable in slop-cop — the defect is in github.com/yasyf/spawnllm/go.

spawnllm's exec.go:69-71 sets cmd.Cancel to SIGTERM cmd.Process alone, with no process group. So when a run times out or its context is cancelled, only the direct child dies; grandchildren survive. Real codex spawns children, so every timed-out LLM pass can leak.

Measured identically before and after the slop-cop-side fix, which proves it is untouched by it:
  === slop-cop ===        after exit: 98657 sleep 600   (count: 1)
  === slop-cop-fixed ===  after exit: 99286 sleep 600   (count: 1)

Fix direction: SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true} at spawn, then syscall.Kill(-pgid, ...) on cancel, in spawnllm's exec.go.

Why this matters beyond tidiness: this machine has been accumulating wedged, zero-CPU, tiny-RSS processes all day (56 /bin/sh at one count, plus slop-cop processes). Two causes were already found and fixed — Homebrew Cask quarantine triggering an unanswered Gatekeeper prompt (slop-cop 0.1.67), and orphaned hook wrappers. This leak is a third candidate source that is still live and would produce exactly that signature: a child left running after its parent was killed, with nobody to reap it.

ops.text: a timed-out LLM invocation leaves no surviving descendant processes
verified by counting descendants after a stub that spawns a long-lived grandchild
